title: 14 Best Natural Wine Bars in Hackney

venues.name: People's Wine
venues.verdict: The highest-rated natural wine bar in Hackney — a true locals' favourite with impeccable French selections.
venues.insiderTip: Ask the staff about bottle provenance — they know every winemaker's story and host regular tastings from incredible regions.
venues.whatToOrder: Try the David & Nathalie Drussé Constellation for a silky, balanced red with prunes and truffle. Also the cheapest oysters in the area.

venues.name: Binch
venues.verdict: A tiny, intimate hidden gem that Reddit and locals adore — great owner, great soundtrack, exceptional wines.
venues.insiderTip: This is a seriously small space, so arrive early on weekends. The owner personally curates every bottle and will guide you through the list.
venues.whatToOrder: Trust the owner's recommendation — the list rotates frequently and every bottle is hand-picked. Pair with their small plates.

venues.name: Weino BIB
venues.verdict: Dalston's favourite — a natural wine taproom and deli championing sustainable formats like boxes and pouches.
venues.insiderTip: Bring a reusable bottle for wine on tap. The deli section has excellent charcuterie to pair with your glass.
venues.whatToOrder: Start with their own Bianco Puglia — a great easy natty white for 'sliding into the evening.' Try the charcuterie board from their in-house deli.

venues.name: Blinds
venues.verdict: Hackney Road's buzzy new addition — natural wine, small plates, and weekend DJs in a beautifully designed space.
venues.insiderTip: Come on a weekend evening for the DJ sets — it transforms from wine bar to a proper East London social scene.
venues.whatToOrder: The small plates menu changes regularly. Start with a glass of pét-nat and work through the by-the-glass list.

venues.name: dan's
venues.verdict: The most approachable natural wine bar in Dalston — candlelit tables, shabby-chic antiques, and a blackboard menu that says 'easy red' instead of terroir jargon.
venues.insiderTip: The blackboard menu skips the name/region/year formula — it reads 'spritzy white', 'easy red', 'funky skinsy', 'advanced natty'. Perfect for wine newcomers.
venues.whatToOrder: If you're new to natural wine, start with the 'easy red' or 'spritzy white'. The charcuterie pairs beautifully.

venues.name: Hector's
venues.verdict: A sleek newcomer that took lower Dalston by storm — think Parisian café meets Italian wine list, with a killer vermouth selection.
venues.insiderTip: Try the Americano vermouth — it's excellent. Grab bar counter seats on weeknights to avoid the crowds.
venues.whatToOrder: The Americano vermouth is a must. Wine list leans Italian and French. Pair with the niche charcuterie selection.

venues.name: 107 Wine Bar
venues.verdict: A Clapton institution — part wine shop, part bar — consistently mentioned across every London natural wine list.
venues.insiderTip: Browse their retail shelves before ordering — you can often try bottles that aren't on the by-the-glass list. Great for taking bottles home too.
venues.whatToOrder: Ask what's open and interesting. The staff are brilliant at matching to your mood. Their orange wine selection is particularly strong.

venues.name: Newcomer Wines
venues.verdict: An importer-turned-bar right opposite Dalston Junction station — the Austrian wine selection is genuinely world-class, and the garden is perfect for summer sessions.
venues.insiderTip: Head straight to the back room for a more intimate atmosphere, or grab the garden on a sunny day. Their Austrian wines are the real star.
venues.whatToOrder: Try any Austrian white from their shelves — the selection is extraordinary. The pét-nat options are always interesting too.

venues.name: Sager + Wilde
venues.verdict: One of the bars that started the entire East London natural wine movement — 10+ years in and still one of the best.
venues.insiderTip: The bar-top made from pavement lights is iconic. Explore their Central and Eastern European selections — Polish, Czech, and Slovenian bottles are growing.
venues.whatToOrder: Splurge here — the list rewards bigger spends. Ask about their French whites and the increasingly impressive Eastern European section.

venues.name: Elliot's
venues.verdict: Restaurant, bar, and natural wine store rolled into one — Mare Street's anchor for low-intervention wines and excellent cooking.
venues.insiderTip: Come for weekend lunch — it's a completely different vibe to the evening service. The wine store section lets you buy bottles to take home at retail prices.
venues.whatToOrder: Order from the wine store side for retail pricing on glasses. The seasonal menu pairs brilliantly with their natural selections.

venues.name: Planque
venues.verdict: A refined Haggerston spot in a converted railway arch — serious wine list paired with equally serious cooking.
venues.insiderTip: Book ahead — this place fills up fast. The converted railway arch space is atmospheric and intimate.
venues.whatToOrder: Let the sommelier guide you. The food menu is designed around wine pairing, so trust their suggestions.

venues.name: Yuki Bar
venues.verdict: Under the arches near Hackney Central — Nordic-Japanese small plates with an unmatched natural wine list at genuinely good value.
venues.insiderTip: The trains overhead shake the whole place — it becomes part of the charm. Come for the wine, not the food prices (which can sting).
venues.whatToOrder: The Dard et Ribo Crozes-Hermitage Rouge is stunning. Wine prices are markedly fairer than most East London spots.

venues.name: Cadet
venues.verdict: The spiritual successor to the legendary P. Franco — French bistro cooking meets carefully curated natural wines from the same team.
venues.insiderTip: Try the brains if it's on the menu. Come for Sunday boozy lunch — the French bistro dishes pair perfectly with an uneventful weekend.
venues.whatToOrder: Start with something carbonic — the staff love Cinsault and other light reds. The rillettes are excellent alongside.

venues.name: Cave Cuvée (Top Cuvée Shoreditch)
venues.verdict: A Parisian-inspired subterranean natural wine bar — the sister venue to Highbury's beloved Top Cuvée.
venues.insiderTip: The underground space feels genuinely Parisian. Part bottle shop, part wine bar — buy retail and drink in at a small corkage.
venues.whatToOrder: Browse the bottle shop shelves and pick something interesting — the staff are happy to open anything for you to try.
